scope.surface: Canonical IP&M filing source and attributed arXiv adapter
scope.notes: All sections and paragraphs received deletion, placement, and redundancy review; central and newly repaired passages are represented explicitly below.

elements.reader_question: What may a discovery system infer about task closure from local acquisition outcomes?
elements.incoming_dependency: Readers know retrieval and stopping systems but not the authority boundary between route stopping and task closure.
elements.contribution: Defines and tests a fail-closed control contract that keeps unresolved material routes open.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Supports bounded use as a control layer while withholding retrieval-superiority and completeness claims.
elements.deletion_consequence: The unavailable-route aggregation result and adverse external boundary would have no standalone scientific account.
elements.placement_reason: The complete argument is the submission object.
elements.representation_reason: A full methods paper is needed to connect semantics, controlled mechanisms, exact contracts, and adverse external diagnostics.

redundancy.reason: No sibling paper owns the acquisition-versus-closure question.

elements.reader_question: What is the method, decisive evidence, adverse result, and boundary?
elements.incoming_dependency: The reader has no repository or series context.
elements.contribution: States the control distinction, controlled and exact-contract evidence, descriptive adverse TREC result, BEIR null mechanism result, and no-superiority boundary.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Prevents the body from being read as a leaderboard or completeness claim.
elements.deletion_consequence: The submission would lack a self-contained evidence and boundary summary.
elements.placement_reason: These are the minimum decision-relevant facts for editorial triage.
elements.representation_reason: One compact paragraph is clearer than bullets or internal status labels.

redundancy.reason: Results recur in the body, but the abstract uniquely supplies a standalone triage summary.

elements.reader_question: What was compared, under what budget, and with what evidential status?
elements.incoming_dependency: The external comparison is needed after controlled and exact-contract evidence.
elements.contribution: Defines the 50-topic matched budget and explicitly classifies the exact analysis rule as post-hoc/descriptive.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Licenses numerical reporting without a false registration claim.
elements.deletion_consequence: Readers could mistake the result for prospectively registered evidence or be unable to interpret the comparator and margins.
elements.placement_reason: Design and provenance status must precede the result.
elements.representation_reason: Prose makes the missing pre-outcome binding and preserved analysis rule explicit without adding a misleading protocol table.

redundancy.reason: Only Methods states why the comparison is descriptive rather than registered.

elements.location: Results: Descriptive TREC-COVID comparison is adverse
elements.reader_question: What directions and magnitudes appear on recall, cost, and head-ranking quality?
elements.incoming_dependency: Methods defines the descriptive status and matched topic unit.
elements.contribution: Reports lower recall, higher reads, favorable nDCG, and the no-superiority interpretation together.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Supports the Discussion's metric-dependent trade-off and adverse external boundary.
elements.deletion_consequence: The paper would hide its strongest external discriminator and its adverse result.
elements.placement_reason: Conclusion-changing adverse evidence belongs in the main Results.
elements.representation_reason: Two short paragraphs keep the three metrics and their incompatible directions visible without a redundant display.

redundancy.reason: This is the only full numerical statement of the external comparison.

elements.reader_question: How should opposing recall, cost, and nDCG results change the paper's claim?
elements.incoming_dependency: Results establishes metric-dependent directions under a post-hoc descriptive rule.
elements.contribution: Explains why the comparison is an external stress test rather than prospective confirmation and why it does not establish superiority.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Constrains the conclusion and successor-study requirement.
elements.deletion_consequence: Readers could overread favorable nDCG or ignore the provenance downgrade.
elements.placement_reason: Interpretation and non-implication belong immediately after the controlled evidence discussion.
elements.representation_reason: A prose paragraph is sufficient; another gate table would imply unwarranted prospective authority.

redundancy.reason: It repeats directions but uniquely explains evidential status and claim consequence.

elements.location: Discussion and limitations: additional probes and unavailable campaigns
elements.reader_question: Which adverse, invalid, or unaccessed outcomes remain outside the main evidence chain?
elements.incoming_dependency: The main controlled, exact-contract, TREC, and BEIR results have been interpreted.
elements.contribution: Retains MetaSyn, AutoResearchBench, screening losses, provider-invalid OpenAIRE, and the unaccessed 48-task campaign at their actual authority levels.
elements.outgoing_dependency: Prevents omitted negatives and unavailable data from being mistaken for favorable evidence.
elements.deletion_consequence: Conclusion-changing negative and cannot-check evidence would disappear from the reader-facing record.
elements.placement_reason: These boundaries alter interpretation but do not need the Results-level numerical detail of the central evidence chain.
elements.representation_reason: Continuous prose avoids the mechanical bullet-style limitation section the author rejected.

redundancy.reason: The paragraph integrates otherwise distributed bounded outcomes into the claim boundary.

elements.reader_question: What survives after all positive, adverse, null, and undetermined evidence is considered?
elements.incoming_dependency: All evidence families and limitations are established.
elements.contribution: Restates the bounded control-method contribution and leaves external benefit and completeness unestablished.
elements.deletion_consequence: The paper would end without a calibrated answer to its opening question.
elements.placement_reason: The final synthesis belongs after availability and limitations.
elements.representation_reason: One narrative paragraph avoids a mechanical list and preserves the claim hierarchy.

redundancy.reason: It repeats central terms but uniquely synthesizes the final evidential terminal.

notes: No paragraph is retained solely because it existed in the long-form research record.
The TREC provenance repair changed evidential status but preserved every reported outcome.
Limitations remain narrative prose rather than a mechanical point list.
